question: According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2020, which state in India has the highest share of limestone production?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajasthan** has the highest share of **limestone production** in India, accounting for about **29%** of the total production in the country.
 
• With **27% **of the total resources, **Karnataka **is the most **resource-rich state**, followed by **Rajasthan** and **Andhra Pradesh (12% each), Gujarat (10%), and Meghalaya (9%).**
 
• **Limestone** is a **sedimentary rock** composed mainly of **calcium carbonate** and is used in various industries, including **cement, steel, and chemicals**.
 
• The two minerals that make up limestone's majority are **aragonite and calcite**, which are distinct crystal forms of **CaCO₃.**
 
• When these minerals separate from water that has dissolved calcium, limestone is created. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telangana** has only a small share of about **1%** of the total production.
 
• **Chhattisgarh** is the** second-largest producer** of limestone in India.
 
 
• It is accounting for about** 17%** of the total production.
 
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** is also a significant producer of limestone.
 
 
• It has a share of about **13% **of the total production.
